title: Fuse large producer/consumer handoffs and align asynchronous RTL returns by launch-local identity
objective: Prevent Scheduler scalar copies from dominating vector DAGs and prevent correct parallel RTL returns from being rejected solely because tiles complete out of order.

rules.statement: When a Venus producer and consumer are compatible in one BAS DAG, connect physical task returns to consumer inputs through direct value dependencies and concat. Treat a payload-sized Scheduler byte/word copy as a rejected performance candidate unless measured end-to-end evidence proves it acceptable.
rules.falsification: Retain a separate Scheduler handoff when fusion violates backend limits, changes visible fixed-point checkpoints, increases the winning end-to-end latency, or requires unsupported address lifetimes.

rules.statement: A fused graph should reference already-qualified task source files through the toolchain task-source manifest. Do not duplicate operator C merely to place it in a new DAG directory.
rules.falsification: A specialization is allowed only when its distinct source is required by measured performance or bit-exactness and is independently qualified.

rules.statement: For a sequence of Scheduler DAG launches, preserve launch order but match returns inside each launch by (task_id, return_port), not by DMA arrival or task-completion order. Record the original sequence index for audit.
rules.falsification: Reject alignment if the launch has duplicate keys, missing keys, unexpected keys, an ambiguous boundary, unknown bytes, or any payload/length mismatch after identity alignment.

rules.statement: Identity alignment changes only comparison ordering. Qualification still requires every visible return, byte, task completion and final OAI output to match, plus successful RTL completion markers and exit status.
rules.falsification: Any aligned data mismatch or missing completion rejects the candidate.

backend_scoped_evidence.workload: OAI NR UE canonical RX1 PBCH time-domain fused application

rejected_scalar_handoff.symptom: FFT and pack completed, then the Scheduler scalar shared-SRAM copy dominated wall time and never launched the product within the retained run

return_order_example.result: all four payload SHA256 values match their launch-local task identities exactly

non_transferable_items: the measured Gem5 and RTL cycle values
promotion_conditions: A second multi-tile DAG showing the same launch-local return-order behavior
A second producer/consumer workload showing a large scalar handoff replaced by exact BAS dependencies
An exact shadow patch against the then-current skill and knowledge digests

shadow_patch.reason: This turn records workload evidence only; portable skill promotion requires the stated second workload and explicit human review.

rollback: Remove this proposal and its index entries; workload code and immutable evidence remain valid.
